In brief: We're expecting a relatively typical week ahead for Abuja, with warm to hot temperatures and a chance of scattered showers and thunderstorms. As we head into the week, a slight increase in moisture could lead to more unsettled weather, particularly towards the latter part of the week. Let's dive deeper into the forecast.

The current conditions in Abuja are quite pleasant, with a temperature of 24°C and a feels-like temperature of 28°C due to the 79% humidity. The winds are light, blowing at 4 km/h, which is not unusual for this time of year. If you're planning on heading out, be sure to check the traffic conditions, especially on major roads like the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway, which is currently experiencing light traffic. As you navigate through the city, you might notice the scenery around you, with the landscape of Abuja's rolling hills and rock formations that make up a significant part of the city's geography.

The geography of Abuja plays a significant role in shaping the local weather patterns. As we head into the week, we can expect the temperatures to rise, with highs reaching into the mid-30s by the time we reach the early part of the week. This heat will be felt across the city, from the bustling streets of Wuse to the more suburban areas of Garki.

### Monday to Wednesday
The start of the week will see mostly dry and sunny conditions, with plenty of sunshine and warm temperatures. This will be an excellent time to get outdoors and enjoy the scenery, whether that's taking a stroll around the National Arboretum or visiting the Aso Rock. However, as we head into the latter part of the week, we can expect a slight increase in moisture, which could lead to more unsettled weather. This might impact travel plans, especially if you're planning on commuting to work or school, so be sure to check the latest forecast before you head out.

### Thursday and Beyond
As we head into the latter part of the week, we can expect to see a significant increase in moisture, which could lead to more unsettled weather.
